text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Jordanian press on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Egypt's President Hosni Mubarak ready to host a four-way Arab summit with Jordan, Syria and the Palestinians.
- King Hussein told a cabinet meeting on Saturday to speed up moves to turn the Red Sea port of Aqaba into a free trade zone to attract investment and tourism.

- Government tells parliamentarians it wants to pass a number of economic laws, including stock exchange law, rapidly and in temporary form without putting them before parliament. MPs want parliament to hold a special session to discuss them.

- Source says Prime Minister Abdul-Salam al-Majali wants to limit bureaucracy facing investors to a maximum of one week. Any investor whose applications take longer than that time would be allowed to bypass the government office holding him up.
- Twelve people discovered with AIDS in Jordan so far this year, bringing the number since 1986 to 148, of which 93 were Jordanians.
- Egypt has not yet contacted Jordan over a possible summit meeting, information minister says.
- Japan's financial aid to Jordan in 1997/98 will be made up of $200 million worth of soft loans, loans with grace periods, and technical assistance.
- Head of General Security denies reports of any hunger strikes at Jordan's Suwaqa jail.
- Industrial Development Bank to get $50 million loan from European Investment Bank to help modernisation.
